title: Interest on Reserve Balances (IORB) - Daily Observation
summary: The Interest on Reserve Balances (IORB) rate held steady at 3.65% on 2026-04-30, unchanged from 2026-04-29. IORB is the interest rate the Federal Reserve pays on reserve balances held by depository institutions, serving as a key policy rate in the Fed's floor system.
key_points: Rate has remained at 3.65% for at least five consecutive observations (2026-04-26 through 2026-04-30)
IORB serves as a floor for overnight interest rates in the federal funds market
why_it_matters: IORB serves as the floor for overnight interest rates in the federal funds market. Banks have no incentive to lend reserves below this rate, making IORB a key determinant of monetary policy transmission to money markets. The rate is typically set at or near the top of the federal funds target range.
market_structure_context: IORB is a core element of the Fed's floor system for monetary policy implementation. By paying interest on reserves, the Fed anchors short-term rates without directly controlling the federal funds market. The current IORB at 3.65% suggests the top of the fed funds target range is approximately 3.50-3.75%. Note: Unlike active balance sheet operations (QE/QT), IORB is an administratively set policy rate reflecting the current policy stance.
